subject: Deployment residency: EU/APAC availability & next steps
messages:
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: lars.johansen@nordbank.com
Date: 2026-10-05T13:12:00-04:00
Subject: Deployment residency: EU/APAC availability & next steps

Hi Lars - thanks again for taking the time this morning.

Recap of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: EU data residency for customer data and logs (GDPR).
- Secondary: Low-latency inference for APAC offices (Singapore) for a subset of EU-hosted models; acceptable to route inference across regions if data residency is guaranteed.
- Likely workloads: real-time chat (low-latency) + batch embeddings for search.

Two clarifying questions: 
1) For EU residency, do you need all inference compute to reside in EU, or is it acceptable if only the data plane/storage is EU while inference runs in APAC for latency-sensitive users?
2) Any procurement constraints pushing toward a private VPC/on-prem deployment (e.g., specific KMS/HSM requirements or local audit controls)?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll loop in our solutions engineer (Monica) and security lead (Neha) for a short technical call to map options (hosted EU, dedicated reserved capacity, private VPC/on-prem).
- If useful, I can share a high-level doc (compliance matrix + topologies) before that call.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: lars.johansen@nordbank.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T15:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Deployment residency: EU/APAC availability & next steps

Hi Marissa - thanks for the recap. Quick answers below and a couple of additional constraints from procurement.

- Residency: We need customer data and logs to remain in the EU for regulatory reporting. Ideally, inference for EU customers should happen in EU compute. For APAC users, we'd prefer routing to nearby regions for latency but only if request payloads and logs can be retained in EU (or anonymized).
- KMS/HSM: Procurement prefers customer-managed keys or HSM integration; full on-prem HSM is not strictly required but we need compatibility with our AWS KMS + external key management.
- SLA/Support: For production volumes we are looking for an SLA and support window that aligns with EU banking hours; may consider dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

Would a short technical call tomorrow with your solutions engineer make sense? Also, can you share the compliance matrix and a simple topology diagram so we can show procurement?

Best,
Lars
Head of Digital Channels
Nordbank

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: lars.johansen@nordbank.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-06T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Deployment residency: EU/APAC availability & next steps

Lars - thanks for the quick clarifications, that helps. Looping in Monica (solutions) and Neha (security) so we can propose 2-3 concrete deployment options for procurement and engineering to review.

Summary of proposed options (high-level):

1) Hosted API (EU region) + cross-region routing for latency:
- Data plane & logs stored in EU (we can restrict storage to eu-west-1 / eu-central-1).
- Short-lived inference requests can be proxied from APAC to EU compute; request payloads are encrypted in transit.
- For strict audit requirements: we can enable request-level logging that stores request metadata in EU only; payloads can be redacted or anonymized.
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, managed upgrades, usage-based pricing.
- Cons: cross-region inference adds latency; must validate procurement on cross-border processing specifics.

2) Dedicated (Reserved Capacity) in EU:
- Dedicated GPU pools and reserved capacity in EU region(s).
- Predictable throughput and enterprise SLA; integrates with customer KMS for key management (we support AWS KMS + customer-managed keys).
- Pros: predictable performance, better alignment with procurement/SLA needs.
- Cons: higher committed cost, provisioning lead time.

3) Private VPC / On-prem option:
- Private control plane with customer-managed network (VPC peering or private link) or fully on-prem packaging for air-gapped needs.
- Supports HSM/KMS integrations and full control of network egress.
- Pros: maximum control for compliance/procurement.
- Cons: longer deployment timeline, higher integration effort and op-ex.

Attachments: I've attached a short compliance matrix and a topology diagram showing Hosted EU + APAC routing and a Dedicated/Private VPC variant to illustrate data flow and where logs are stored.

Suggested next steps:
- 30-45 minute technical call with Monica and Neha to walk the preferred option and procurement questions.
- If Dedicated or Private is preferred, we'll prepare a cost/lead-time estimate.

Proposed times (CET friendly): Wed 6 Oct 11:00-11:45 CET or Thu 7 Oct 14:00-14:45 CET. Does either work for you?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
